thread_pair_example: driver ./main 64 64 192 192 1 (hsize = vsize = selSize = 64 -> blocks of 64 threads = 2 warps), vhgw_horiz, any block, offset = 1: thread 31 (warp 0) writes opArray[31 + 64 - 1] = opArray[94] (L94) while thread 32 (warp 1) reads opArray[32 + 64 - 1 - 1] = opArray[94] (L95); the barrier is only at the end of the iteration (L100). Mirrored cross-warp pair in the reverse scan (L98, not listed as a site): thread 32 writes opArray[32] while thread 31 reads opArray[31 + 1] = opArray[32] (threads 33/34 give the same pair inside warp 1). vhgw_vert has the same pairs with threadIdx.y as tid (block (1,64)).
class_reason: plain unsigned char accesses in dynamic shared memory by different warps with no barrier between the read of an iteration and the in-place write by another thread: DR. Single-byte accesses; the conflicting addresses are identical bytes.
buggy_expected: the pair (write L94 vs read L95, plus the reverse-scan pair L98 vs L98) is reported as DR (RAW/WAR across warps on opArray bytes), in all four kernel instances; for selSize <= 32 only an intra-warp lock-step pair would remain (not exercised by this driver).

fixed.reason: the fix (7be8747e) rewrites the loop into a read phase into registers (L102-L103), __syncthreads (L105), then a write phase (L107-L108), with a __syncthreads (L100) at the start of every iteration, so no read of opArray in an iteration is concurrent with a write of the same iteration (verify.expected_report_fixed).

The fixed build: LDS L102/L103 (0x02a0-0x02d0 in vhgw_vert), BAR.SYNC at L105 (0x0310), STS at L107/L108 (0x0330/0x0350), BAR.SYNC at L100 (0x0250).

open_questions: Accesses are single bytes: a detector with word-granular shadow memory may merge neighbouring bytes written by different threads into extra (false) pairs; the true conflicts are on identical byte addresses (verify.notes).
The driver is 192x192 (reporter: 512x512); the 128x128 image prints FAIL in both variants (the app's own result check depends on the border), 130..256 PASS.

review.notes: Checked at e245737: twoWayScan (morphology.cu:82-102) is inlined into vhgw_horiz (:105-134, block (hsize,1)) and vhgw_vert (:137-170, block (1,vsize)) (:189-199); the forward step writes opArray[tid+selSize-1] (:94) and reads opArray[tid+selSize-1-offset] (:95), which thread tid-offset writes in the same iteration; the only barrier per iteration is :100. Plain unsigned char dynamic shared memory: DR. Intra-warp pairs exist as well. Fixed 7be8747: read phase into registers (:102-103), __syncthreads (:105), write phase (:107-108), __syncthreads at the start of every iteration (:100). The loop now ends without a barrier, but for selSize = 64 the last iteration (offset 32) writes only opArray[tid] (tid <= 31) and opArray[tid+63] (tid >= 32), exactly the elements each thread itself reads after the scan (vhgw_horiz :140; vhgw_vert likewise), so no pair remains: 'absent' holds. The driver deviates from the CLAUDE.md table (128x128), as recorded in open_questions. sass_notes are the builder's: the reviewer read sources and diffs only and did not re-dump SASS (the one srun queued with an estimated start the next day and was withdrawn).
